\title{When Does Edge AI Defect Inspection Pay Back Its Carbon? Measured Embedded Inference, Detector Recall, and Alert Design}

\author{Utkarsh~Sengar%
\thanks{U.~Sengar is an Independent Researcher, Dharwad, Karnataka, India (e-mail: sengar.utkarsh2005@gmail.com).}}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Edge AI inspection is often assumed to be green because it prevents scrap; critics point to the electricity of always-on inference. We test both with a conservation-checked, consequential accounting model that compares four edge-AI alert policies and three textbook alarm baselines with no inspection and with manual inspection in three reference scenarios. Its inputs are measured or sourced: the power of a PatchCore pipeline at 30~FPS on an embedded \JetsonModel{} (\JetsonFullTotalPower~W, whole module) and a workstation GPU, the recall of four detector configurations on all \DetCategories{} MVTec~AD and VisA categories, alert rates of our companion alarm study on MVTec~AD and held-out VisA images, and public life-cycle data. In the reference scenarios the edge cell is at most \EdgeOfBenefitMax\% of the benefit; it matters only where the benefit is small. Against no inspection, edge AI emits less in every Monte Carlo draw of the reference scenarios; a rule decides: inspect when the defective parts produced per hour carry more embodied carbon than the cell emits per hour (about \NomogramGramsPerHour~gCO$_2$e). Against manual inspection the answer depends on the line: with benchmark recall at a strict threshold (median \DetPcVisaRecallMedian{} on VisA) the full alert policy emits less in \McProbLMin--\McProbLMax\% of draws, and detector recall explains \RecallSobolMin--\RecallSobolMax{} of the variance. On held-out VisA images its persistence filter misses \VisaRecallLossFull\% of the defects raw thresholding flags, and it emits less in only \VisaMcProbLMin--\VisaMcProbLMax\% of draws. Doubling input resolution raises median recall to \CrHiresRecall{}, repaid at least \CrHiresPaybackMin-fold. Alert design must preserve recall on weak defect scores.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
Sustainable manufacturing, edge AI, industrial anomaly detection, energy measurement, carbon accounting, alarm management, uncertainty analysis.
\end{IEEEkeywords}
